RB.label: Projectable starters end here. Have 3 RBs by pick ~50 in a 2-FLEX league.
Beyond here you are buying injury insurance and lottery tickets.

TE.label: Sharp drop after the top 2, then a long flat plateau. Elite-or-wait.

QB.label: Josh Allen is his own tier; the next tier goes ~25 picks later. Never reach.

WR.label: Top-tier thins out but WR stays draftable deep. Don't chase if you miss.

heuristics.rule: Recommend the LAST player in a breaking tier over the highest-ranked player available when the next tier starts within the user's next-pick window.
With 2 FLEX slots, weight RB/WR depth above a marginal upgrade at QB or TE.
Never suggest a kicker. Surface the extra bench slot as a handcuff or second DST recommendation.
McBride/Bowers ADP has fallen into Round 4 while expert ranks put them ~17th and ~24th overall. Flag as a structural edge when either is available after pick 30.
Do not recommend QB before pick ~50 unless Josh Allen falls past his ADP by 8+ picks.
Recommend exactly one DST in the last two rounds, prioritizing Weeks 1-4 schedule over season-long ranking.
If a rostered RB has risk_score >= 4 or an injury_tag, surface his handcuff.
Warn when 3+ projected starters share a bye, especially Week 11 (6 teams off).
A player is only a value if ADP has fallen to compensate for the injury. Flag cases where risk rose but ADP did not (e.g. Jeremiyah Love, Alec Pierce).

value_calc.vorp_note: Compute replacement level per position using league starters: RB/WR replacement should account for the 2 FLEX slots (approx RB30 / WR30 in a 12-team 2-FLEX league), TE12, QB12, DST12.

draft_slot_1_plan.structural_note: Picks 24 and 25 are back-to-back. Plan in pairs.

picks_24_25.rule: Take one from each group. McBride at 25 is defensible because he will not last to 48.
